Runner A bundles Go 1.21.3, uses the standard auto setting, and builds a main module with go 1.21.0 plus toolchain go1.21.9; no go1.21.9 executable is on PATH. Explain each runner's expected selection or refusal and distinguish the go and toolchain directives, including what a dependency's suggestion does to downstream consumers. Someone proposes GOSUMDB=off to make automatic toolchain downloads work in restricted CI, and claims +path makes the entire build network-free. I have both key pages. Let me analyze the three runners.

Runner A: bundled Go 1.21.3, GOTOOLCHAIN=auto (standard), main module go.mod: go 1.21.0 + toolchain go1.21.9. No go1.21.9 on PATH.

Selection: default toolchain = local (bundled 1.21.3). toolchain line go1.21.9 is newer than default → runs go1.21.9. No go1.21.9 in PATH → downloads and verifies it. Download requires network; if GOSUMDB=off, toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification. Note: go line 1.21.0 is older than bundled 1.21.3, but toolchain line takes precedence when newer.

Runner B: bundled Go 1.21.3, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, module go line 1.21.9. GOTOOLCHAIN=local: always runs bundled toolchain (1.21.3). Module declares go 1.21.9 > 1.21.3 → the toolchain refuses to load module: "Go toolchains refuse to load a module or workspace that declares a minimum required Go version greater than the toolchain's own version." So Runner B fails/refuses. GOTOOLCHAIN=local never downloads.

Wait — also need to consider that when GOTOOLCHAIN=local, the go command always runs bundled toolchain; the bundled 1.21.3 then refuses since go line 1.21.9 requires newer. Yes, refusal.

Runner C: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.3+path, module go 1.21.0 + toolchain go1.21.9, same PATH (no go1.21.9). Default toolchain go1.21.3; toolchain line go1.21.9 newer → go command runs go1.21.9; searches PATH; not found; +path disables download fallback → error. So Runner C fails. Note: with +path, the go command scans PATH for toolchain executables; none found → error like "no such toolchain go1.21.9" / toolchain not found. Documented: "Using the GOTOOLCHAIN form <name>+path disables the download fallback, causing the go command to stop after searching the executable path." So refusal to switch: error.

go vs toolchain directives:
- go line: minimum required Go version to use the module; mandatory since Go 1.21; also sets language version enforced per module; must be >= go lines of all required dependency modules.
- toolchain line: suggested toolchain; only takes effect when module is the main module and default toolchain is older; ignored when module is a dependency ("Only takes effect when the module is the main module"). Also implicit toolchain line = go line version.

Dependency's suggestion effect on downstream consumers: when a dependency module's go.mod has a go line newer, go get/tidy bump the main module go line; and when a command encounters a dependency requiring newer go, toolchain switches (with auto/path). But the toolchain line of a dependency is ignored (toolchain line only takes effect for main module). So a dependency's toolchain suggestion does NOT switch downstream consumers' toolchains; only its go line matters (as a minimum requirement). Consumers' commands like go get or builds with auto may switch based on dependency go lines.

GOSUMDB=off claim: toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification if GOSUMDB=off. So GOSUMDB=off doesn't make downloads work — it breaks them. Documented in the download section: "toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification if GOSUMDB=off." So the proposal is wrong.

+path network-free claim: +path disables download fallback but the build may still need network for module downloads (dependencies) unless modules are cached/vendored/proxied. +path only removes toolchain download; module fetches still need GOPROXY/network. So claim is wrong — +path only constrains toolchain selection to PATH; it doesn't make the whole build network-free. Also, with +path, if toolchain needed is not on PATH, the build fails. UNVERIFIED specifics: whether go.mod/go.sum caching means zero network — depends on module cache.

Policy recommendation: For restricted CI:
- Keep verification: don't set GOSUMDB=off; toolchain downloads are checksum-verified via the Go checksum database; toolchain downloads fail if GOSUMDB=off.
- Options: (1) install/pin the needed toolchain on PATH (then +path or auto finds it locally); (2) pre-populate toolchain module cache with a verified download (e.g., warm cache from a mirror with proxy + sumdb); (3) set GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.21.9 (specific name) — hmm, that downloads if not found on PATH. Actually with GOTOOLCHAIN=<name>, if binary not found in PATH, it downloads and verifies. So same network issue.
- Set module's go/toolchain lines to match available toolchain: keep go line as minimum (e.g., go 1.21.0) and toolchain line as preference; publish with go line low enough for consumers.
- For CI, GOTOOLCHAIN=local with a runner whose bundled version >= module go line is fine, but the runner version must be kept >= go line; else refusal.

Guarantees not established: GOTOOLCHAIN=local doesn't guarantee the build succeeds if go line newer than bundled; auto doesn't guarantee network-free; GOSUMDB=off breaks toolchain downloads (not enables). No guarantee that toolchain line affects dependencies. Also language version enforcement: go line sets language version; using newer toolchain with go 1.21.0 still enforces 1.21 language version.
